title: Earth's Deadliest Predator From Every Single Period
format: 16:9 long-form, 854x480 @30fps source, 32m15s, single narrator VO over a fast collage of licensed/credited paleoart stills, documentary/CG b-roll, live-animal stock, diagrams and meme clips; no chapters in description

chapters_inferred.title: Cold open: hardest game ever = game of life

title_pattern.template: Earth's Deadliest [Category] From Every Single [Time Unit]
title_pattern.type: superlative x exhaustive-series list ('X from every Y'), sequel to the channel's own sea-animal version
title_pattern.notes: Promise = a ranked bracket through deep time; 'Every Single' signals completeness and long watch time; 'Deadliest' is the morbid hook. Implicit open loop: who wins the present period (answer: you/humans). Title case, no number, no emoji. Franchise-able: same frame was used for sea animals and is reused for land.

thumbnail.composition: Dark night-time diorama: 8 champion predators from the video (T. rex, Anteosaurus, giant short-faced bear rearing, Allosaurus head, Fasolasuchus, Barinasuchus, gorgonopsid, Pulmonoscorpius) packed into a lineup in tall grass, filling left 3/4 of frame; a dark silhouetted human with a flashlight in the right foreground beams light onto the giant scorpion in the centre.
thumbnail.colours: Low-key dark green/charcoal background, warm desaturated flesh/khaki animal tones, single cool-white flashlight cone as the brightest element; very little saturated colour.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Human silhouette is foreground-large but faceless; the T. rex towers top-left, the bear stands upright like a person. The tiny-but-lit scorpion vs giant unlit T. rex creates a 'which is deadliest?' puzzle; the human as observer foreshadows the 'go find a mirror' ending.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads as a 'line-up of monsters' at thumbnail size, promises many creatures (value), horror-movie flashlight framing adds tension and a viewer stand-in. The lit scorpion is an odd focal choice that sparks curiosity. No text needed because the title carries the premise.

hook.verbatim: We like to think of games like Elden Ring, Dark Souls, Getting Over It, or Cuphead as being hard, but in reality, the hardest game ever created is the game of life.
hook.device: Pop-culture reframe / false-premise correction: rapid 2s cuts of famous hard video games, then pivot to 'game of life'. Followed by a 'battle royale' frame (0:34) and a series-callback ('just like my other video about the deadliest sea animals'). Promise of a winner per period sets an open loop that pays off on the final line.
hook.visuals: 0:00 Elden Ring key art, 0:02 Getting Over It, 0:04 Cuphead, 0:06 molten early Earth, then sea / sky / land b-roll matching 'swam / flew / walked', 0:32-0:39 big collage of every-era predators charging at camera.

beats.summary: Hard video games -> hardest game is the game of life; 4 billion years of competitors; 'swam/flew/walked' tricolon; question: deadliest terrestrial predator of every period.
Battle Royale framing; callback to the sea-animal video; rules: start in the Cambrian 538 Mya, fully terrestrial animals only.
Zero land contenders; a microorganism is 'top dog' by default (crown on a microbe). Sets the joke tone and the escalation curve.
Arthropod trackways disqualified (needed water); plants/fungi as honorary winners; time-traveller stubs toe joke (Family Guy clip). '100 million years blasted through' counter.
First land animals = myriapods; tiny detritivore millipede from Scotland as potential winner. 'Not so scary, I know' - promises it will escalate.

'New sheriff in town': primitive spider-like arachnids, first true land predators; no silk, no venom, clasp-knife fangs, liquefy prey; spread across Laurentia/Gondwana. Teases a possible back-to-back win.
Tiktaalik (not terrestrial), giant aquatic scorpion Praearcturus (foot-long, disqualified), single lunged scorpion specimen caveat, tiny Devonobius centipede; verdict stays with trigonotarbids.
Age of insects; house-cat-sized 70 cm scorpion, fist-sized stinger; myth-bust on venom vs size (pincer-to-tail ratio chart); synapsids rising; Carboniferous rainforest collapse as the transition.
Gorgonopsids (300 kg sabre-teeth) set up as the obvious answer, then subverted: Anteosaurus 6 m / 600 kg, Kodiak-bear comparison, head-butting, global range; ends with Capitanian extinction.
Great Dying wipes 95% of species - 'reset the competition'; size train speeds up afterwards.
'Contrary to what you might believe, not a dinosaur': 10 m, 3 t quadruped rauisuchid 'kaiju', armour, designed to take down 12 t sauropods; Triassic-Jurassic extinction hands the world to dinosaurs.

beats.beat_type: segment: Jurassic - tie Allosaurus anax / Torvosaurus gurneyi
beats.summary: Tie verdict; species-level nuance (Panthera analogy), 12 m each, agility vs powerhouse, slash vs crush; 'not if they can kill you but how'; Tithonian minor extinction.

Escalation peak: lists Giganotosaurus, Spinosaurus etc. then 'you know exactly who'; size 13 m, 9-12 t (15 polar bears), 57,000 N bite 'pop the skull like a Gusher', arms, smell/vision, brain; asteroid 'coincidence' joke.

'Age of mammals' misnomer: the winner is still a reptile, a terrestrial sebecid 'land croc' 10 m / 1-2 t, ziphodont teeth + armour ('Hannah Montana, best of both worlds'). Caveat on dating, runner-ups Dentaneosuchus, Hyainailouros, Andrewsarchus.
Consolation prize for mammals: largest bear ever, 1.5-2+ t, 4.3 m rearing (giraffe), 'Ron Swanson' hypercarnivore; prey list; battle scars; hibernation 'never set foot in a cave'.
Quaternary: deadliest predator now 'and possibly of all time' - 'drop a like, subscribe, and then go find yourself a mirror.' Twist ending folded into CTA, outro.

pacing.transcript_note: YouTube auto-subs (en); speech runs 0:00-32:12 nearly continuously, no pauses or music breaks.
pacing.shot_length_note: Estimated from 2s frame sampling: roughly 55-65 distinct visuals per 4 minutes (about 3-5 s each; noun-matched cuts drop to 2 s in lists). ffmpeg scene detection (threshold 0.12) finds only about 206 hard cuts (about 9.4 s) because most transitions are soft blur dissolves and many segments are Ken Burns moves on stills.
pacing.period_card_interval_s: about 140 s on average (14 period cards in 32 min), each a re-hook and progress marker
pacing.re_hook_devices: New-winner reveal every 2-4 min, 'contrary to what you might believe' subversions, joke every ~30-45 s, stat badges every ~60 s

art_style: Collage explainer: credited third-party paleoart stills (artist name bottom-right), documentary CG clips, live-animal stock, scientific figures on white floating cards with soft drop shadow over blurred full-bleed background, plus a consistent overlay kit: giant 3D extruded condensed caps period titles, geologic-time ruler, circular icon badges (weight kettlebell, length ruler, bone) with condensed white stat text, white silhouette size charts with human scale figure.
techniques_worth_copying: Exhaustive chronological bracket ('every single period') = built-in progress bar and completion drive; viewers stay to see the next winner.
Deliberate anticlimax start (microbe and plant 'winners') used as comedy and to set up a steep escalation curve to T. rex.
Subversion beats: set up the obvious answer (gorgonopsids, dinosaurs, mammals) then reveal the real winner.
Every size claim is grounded in a familiar reference: house cat, Kodiak bear, giraffe, 15 polar bears, a car, your fist.
Reusable stat-badge system (icon circle + number) and silhouette-vs-human size cards; numbers sometimes update live (46,206 -> 57,000 N; 2018 -> 2011).
Period title cards on a persistent geologic-timeline ruler: chaptering without YouTube chapters.
Pop-culture similes and meme inserts every 30-45 s (Elden Ring blood priest, Hannah Montana, Ron Swanson, Gusher, Family Guy) keep tone light at 200 wpm.
Disqualification/rules segments (must be fully terrestrial) add credibility and debate bait for comments.
Twist CTA: the final 'deadliest predator' is the viewer - 'go find yourself a mirror' - which ties the hook's open loop to the subscribe ask.
code_only_remake_needs: Original creature art: SVG/vector paleoart for ~15 hero animals (side-profile silhouettes + a flat-shaded colour version), since we cannot use stock or credited paleoart; parallax layered SVG landscapes per period (swamp, desert, plain, forest) with Ken Burns camera.

Period title card component: huge 3D-ish extruded condensed caps text (CSS text-shadow stack or SVG), blur-in animation, plus a geologic-time ruler bar with ticks (Mya) and period bands that slides to the current interval.
Stat badge component: circular icon (weight, length, bite, bone) + condensed number with count-up and value-swap animation; units dual (metric | imperial).
Size comparison card: white grid card, human silhouette, creature silhouette scaled from real dimensions, reference objects (cat, bear, giraffe, car, polar bear grid with morph into one silhouette).
Floating 'figure card' component: white rounded card with drop shadow over a blurred full-bleed backdrop, for diagrams, cladograms, maps.
Paleo-globe/map component with continent shapes per era, glowing region fill and pulsing location rings.
Kinetic counters: '100 MILLION YEARS', '95%' ring gauge, extinction titles in red with ember/fire particle overlay (canvas).
Transitions: soft blur/zoom dissolves and white flash for extinction events; cut-on-noun timing driven by word timestamps from TTS.
Gag inserts replaced with original simple vector gags (crown on microbe, red X, stubbed toe stick figure).
TTS at ~190-200 wpm with energetic delivery; animated like/subscribe button outro.
A 32-minute runtime is long for a pilot; a 8-12 min 'every era' version with 6-8 winners would test the format.
